routes.description: Establish that an unlimited, value-supreme, personal necessary foundation unifies ultimate reality and explains irreducible mind with fewer independent primitives.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if supremacy yields the relevant attributes without added fundamental complexity and better unifies necessary reality, value, and consciousness.

motionBridge.description: Show that a supreme personal foundation better accounts for ultimate reality, mind, and worldview simplicity than a nonmental initial reality.

centralBridges.description: Show that removing arbitrary foundational limits supports supreme value and its substantive implications.
Show that one supreme foundation explains multiple necessary domains with fewer independent primitives.
Show that consciousness has irreducible features predicted and producible by a supreme mental foundation.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Justify using philosophical evidence from logic, value, mathematics, and consciousness alongside physical evidence.
Preserve focused comparisons of theoretical virtues while situating them within the complete worldview comparison.

routes.description: Establish that a necessary nonmental initial reality, continuous with later nature, avoids unwarranted primordial mentality and explains minds through neural functioning.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if foundational mentality and supremacy remain additional commitments while naturalistic continuity, neural identity, and total-package comparison remain adequate.

motionBridge.description: Show that a naturalistic initial reality better accounts for ultimate reality, evolved mind, and total worldview simplicity than a supreme personal foundation.

centralBridges.description: Characterize the necessary initial reality as causally continuous with later nature without primordial mentality.
Show that mentality and divine attributes add substantive structure not obtained merely by removing limits.
Show that appropriately situated neural functioning can fully account for conscious states.
Require simplicity and explanatory fit to be assessed across the complete disputed commitments of each worldview.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Require adequate evidence before assigning rich properties to the unknown initial reality.
Allow logic, morality, value, and physical origins to have independent foundations rather than one common source.

sections.title: Category and continuity of initial reality
sections.rationale: The characterization of the necessary initial reality determines whether the comparison requires an additional ontological category or permits continuity with later concrete reality.

sections.title: Unlimited supremacy and foundational complexity
sections.rationale: The central simplicity dispute turns on whether an unlimited supreme nature reduces arbitrary specification or instead introduces mentality and unsupported divine consequences.

sections.title: Evidence, necessity, and explanatory unification
sections.rationale: This issue determines whether cross-domain evidence warrants a unified supreme source or whether necessary physical and nonphysical domains may terminate separately.

sections.title: Nature and source of consciousness
sections.rationale: The motion's mind component depends on whether consciousness is irreducible evidence for a mental foundation or identical with evolved neural functioning.

sections.title: Scope of the worldview comparison
sections.rationale: The comparative burden requires a method for relating focused simplicity and explanatory questions to the broader balance of disputed worldview commitments.

moves.speaker: Graham Oppy
moves.proposition: Once shared causal history and ordinary composition are held fixed, the principal worldview disagreement concerns the character of the necessary initial reality.
moves.attributionBasis: Rasmussen's preceding question explicitly addresses Graham, and this sustained answer ends before Rasmussen resumes the inquiry about fundamentality.

response.rationale: This constructive move usefully isolates the initial-reality dispute, though it does not itself settle the comparative explanatory question.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within constructive moves, it efficiently frames a material issue but offers only a compressed argument for treating other history as shared.

precisionFindings.rationale: The principal-disagreement claim is recoverable and stable, with the shared-history condition reasonably clear but partly implicit.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The passage cautiously presents the focus as a comparative framing judgment and acknowledges possible disagreement near the causal beginning.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The narrowing inference is coherent, though it assumes without full defense that later causal and compositional history is substantially shared.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: Shared examples such as cats support the framing, but the representativeness of that agreement across the full worldview remains compressed.

relevanceBurden.rationale: The move directly supports the central naturalistic task of locating the indispensable dispute in the character of initial reality.

representationalCharity.rationale: No developed opposing interpretation is directly assessed, so the neutral charity anchor applies.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt says the parties need not disagree about ordinary causal history and locates uncertainty near the beginning of that history.

moves.speaker: Josh Rasmussen
moves.proposition: A necessary foundational reality may count as natural when it is intelligible, scientifically investigable, and in the same basic category as other concrete things.
moves.attributionBasis: The passage follows Oppy's historical account, directly addresses Graham, and continues Rasmussen's earlier first-person inquiry about the term natural.

response.rationale: This constructive move supplies criteria under which a necessary foundation may remain natural and categorically continuous with concrete reality.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within constructive moves, it gives several explicit category criteria, though their sufficiency for naturalness is not fully defended.

precisionFindings.rationale: The criteria are explicit, but natural shifts among scientific accessibility, intelligibility, nonmagical character, and categorical sameness.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The modest claim that such a foundation may count as natural fits the illustrative support and does not overstate a definition.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The listed properties can coherently motivate classification as natural, but their connection to one basic category remains partly stipulative.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The orange-foundation example illustrates conceptual possibility, but it does not establish that scientific investigability and intelligibility are sufficient criteria.

relevanceBurden.rationale: The move materially supports the subsidiary category comparison but does not complete the motion-level explanatory comparison.

representationalCharity.rationale: The move proposes a classification without materially characterizing a developed opposing alternative.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt expressly identifies scientific investigation, intelligibility, rational accessibility, and categorical continuity as marks of naturalness.

moves.speaker: Graham Oppy
moves.proposition: A naturalistic initial reality is necessary yet causally continuous with later reality, whereas some theologies introduce sharper discontinuities between God and creation.
moves.attributionBasis: The turn immediately answers Rasmussen's request for alignment and is followed by Rasmussen acknowledging the point and discussing his theological sympathies.

components.text: Whether the necessary foundation belongs to the same basic category as later concrete reality.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: This is a partial answer contacting the decisive category-continuity component while leaving the proposed naturalness criteria untreated.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The initial state's details are acknowledged as open, though causal unfolding alone slightly overstates the assurance of no radical categorical difference.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt calls the initial state's details open while insisting it is not radically distinct because later reality causally unfolds from it.

moves.speaker: Josh Rasmussen
moves.proposition: Among limited, unlimited, and noncommittal descriptions of the necessary initial item, specified arbitrary limits add commitments while agnosticism initially minimizes them.

moves.attributionBasis: The passage directly answers Rasmussen's request for Oppy's view and ends when Rasmussen interrupts to refine the question about naturalism.

components.text: Whether an unlimited foundational description merely removes limits or introduces further substantive properties.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: This partial answer contacts the decisive unlimitedness component explicitly but does not address every option in the three-way comparison.

precisionFindings.rationale: The distinction between removing a quantitative limit and adding mentality is clear, though the extent of added structure is implicit.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The claim is framed as a considered judgment rather than certainty and is proportionate to the conceptual distinction drawn.

relevanceBurden.rationale: The move directly advances the central naturalistic claim that primordial mentality is a substantive additional commitment.

components.text: Whether specified limitations, unlimitedness, or agnosticism is descriptively simplest for the initial reality.

components.text: Whether a supreme mental nature adds qualitative structure beyond the mere removal of arbitrary limits.

Whether the character of the necessary initial reality is the principal comparative disagreement.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt contrasts information-heavy limits with the simple description supreme and treats supreme-making attributes as ensuing predictions.

components.text: Whether supreme value entails the further divine attributes without additional fundamental commitments.
Whether an unlimited description avoids the information needed to specify arbitrary limits.
Whether intelligibility and investigability place a necessary foundation within the natural category.

components.text: Whether rich properties of initial reality may be inferred from a simple supreme description before further evidence.

Whether scientific investigability is a criterion for treating a foundation as natural.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: It fully contacts the epistemic demand behind positive foundational attribution, though it does not refute every conceptual simplicity claim.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The cautious force closely fits the stated evidential uncertainty and avoids claiming that science will necessarily resolve initial properties.

relevanceBurden.rationale: The move directly advances the subsidiary epistemic-restraint burden by limiting positive claims about unknown initial reality.

representationalCharity.rationale: The move states an evidential policy without developing or distorting a specific opposing alternative.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt says science may provide access to the initial properties, allows that they may remain unknowable, and resists positive commitment.

components.text: Whether evidence about the initial foundation must await or principally depend upon fundamental physical science.
Whether supreme value actually entails the claimed logical, moral, mathematical, and personal attributes.
Whether mentality constitutes added qualitative structure rather than mere limit removal.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: This partial answer contacts the evidential-route component but leaves the decisive entailment objections to its cross-domain claims untreated.

precisionFindings.rationale: The evidential domains are identifiable, but evidence, deduction, prediction, and useful data are used without fully distinguishing their roles.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The availability of nonphysical evidence is plausible, while the purported deductions are stronger than the warrants supplied in this span.

relevanceBurden.rationale: The move directly supports the subsidiary cross-domain-evidence bridge by challenging an exclusively scientific evidential route.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt names logic, morality, mathematics, person-building resources, and physics as potentially relevant data for foundational theorizing.

components.text: Whether evidence across logic, value, mathematics, and consciousness supports one common supreme foundation.
Whether a unified supreme nature derives multiple domains with fewer fundamental commitments.
Whether unlimitedness is simpler than independently necessary domains.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: It explicitly contacts the unification demand and supplies a clear contrary model, although the comparative simplicity of that model remains undefended.

precisionFindings.rationale: The physical causal boundary and the independent logical and moral foundations are clearly distinguished, with expectations presented as such.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The speaker frames independence as an expectation rather than a demonstrated necessity, fitting the limited supporting argument.

components.text: Whether necessary logical, moral, physical, and mental domains may adequately terminate in independent foundations.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: It contacts the decisive independence and termination claims, but only partially answers the full challenge because the proposed unifier's entailments remain unstated.

relevanceBurden.rationale: The move directly advances the central unification bridge by contesting independent termination and proposing fewer necessary primitives.
